newsitem.title: USA: Time Inc. New Media teams with AT&T WorldNet.
newsitem.headline: Time Inc. New Media teams with AT&T WorldNet.

text.p: Two American business giants teamed up in cyberspace Wednesday as Time Inc. New Media and AT&T Corp. announced AT&T's Internet service was syndicating online content from such magazines as Time, Sports Illustrated and Money.
No financial details of the deal were disclosed.

Beginning Wednesday, AT&T Worldnet Service subscribers can view online versions of Time, Sports Ilustrated and Money, as well as Fortune and Entertainment Weekly, on featured sections of AT&T Worldnet Web pages, the companies said.
The public also will be able to view the online magazines via the public AT&T Worldnet Service Web site, available at http://www.att.net.
Bridgewater, N.J.-based AT&T Worldnet has 800,000 subscribers, making it the largest pure Internet access service.
The deal moves it further away from providing just Internet access and makes it more of a content provider like bigger commercial online services CompuServe Corp. and America Online Inc.
The content comes from Time Inc. New Media's Pathfinder Web site (http://www.pathfinder.com), one of the earliest and most comprehensive major media outposts on the Web.

"A syndication relationship like this with AT&T confirms the strength of our brands and their value on the Web," Linda McCutcheon, Time Inc. New Media vice president for sales and marketing, said in a statement.

Members of the public will initially see the same Time content on the public Web site as Worldnet subscribers see on members-only Web pages, Worldnet spokesman Jonathan Varman said in a telephone interview. But subscribers should see more, exclusive content within 30 to 60 days, he said.

Until recently, other Time Inc. content was available via CompuServe. But CompuServe dropped Time, which sued CompuServe. The Time information had been available on CompuServe since November 1995, when Time deserted No. 1 online service America Online for No. 2 CompuServe.
Time Inc. New Media is a unit of media conglomerate Time Warner Inc.
Time Warner stock dipped 87.5 cents to $42.625 and AT&T dipped 62.5 cents to $34.25 in consolidated trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
